general_skills.title: Systematic Exploration
general_skills.principle: Search every plausible surface or container exactly once before revisiting; prioritize unopened or unseen locations to cover the whole room methodically.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Anytime the goal object count is not yet met and unexplored locations remain.

general_skills.title: Immediate Acquisition
general_skills.principle: As soon as a required object becomes visible and reachable, take it before moving elsewhere to avoid losing track or re-searching.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Upon first visual confirmation of a goal-relevant object.

general_skills.title: Destination First Policy
general_skills.principle: After picking up a goal object, navigate directly to the known target receptacle and place it before resuming further search.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Holding any goal object while its target location has been identified.

general_skills.title: Track Counts & Progress
general_skills.principle: Maintain an internal counter of how many goal objects are still needed; stop searching or terminate episode only when the counter reaches zero.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Throughout multi-instance tasks (e.g., “put two X…”).

general_skills.title: Use State-Changing Tools Early
general_skills.principle: For tasks requiring heated/cooled/clean objects, acquire the object, then immediately use the nearest suitable appliance to change its state before any placement.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After picking up an object that must change temperature or cleanliness.

general_skills.title: Establish Spatial Relations
general_skills.principle: When a goal specifies a relation (under/inside/on), first locate the reference object, adjust its state if needed (e.g., turn lamp on), then search the specified spatial region for the target object or place it there.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Tasks containing spatial prepositions like under, inside, on, in_front_of.

general_skills.title: Open Before Judging Empty
general_skills.principle: Treat any closed container as unexplored; open it and inspect contents before deciding that the goal object is absent.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Encountering a closed drawer, cabinet, fridge, microwave, etc.

general_skills.title: Avoid Redundant Rechecks
general_skills.principle: Record which locations and containers have been fully inspected; do not revisit them unless new evidence suggests their contents changed.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After the first full pass of a location or when considering next search target.

general_skills.title: Plan with Landmarks
general_skills.principle: Continuously update and reference a map of known object and container locations to choose shortest paths and prevent aimless wandering.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Each time a new furniture piece, container, or goal object is observed.

general_skills.title: Progressive Goal Decomposition
general_skills.principle: Break tasks into ordered sub-goals: (1) locate object, (2) obtain or transform it, (3) locate destination/reference object, (4) satisfy spatial relation/placement, completing each sub-goal before moving to the next.
general_skills.when_to_apply: At the start of every episode and whenever the environment state invalidates the current sub-goal.

general_skills.title: Efficient Relation Search
general_skills.principle: When the goal pairs two objects (A under/on/inside B), restrict search for A to locations near B and vice-versa, instead of treating them independently.
general_skills.when_to_apply: On goals that mention both a target object and a reference object.

general_skills.title: Terminate Only On Success
general_skills.principle: Issue the 'done' action exclusively after validating that all goal conditions are met; otherwise continue searching or correcting object states.
general_skills.when_to_apply: Before ending an episode or when the agent believes the task is complete.

general_skills.title: Station Action Execution
general_skills.principle: When at the required transformation station and holding the object, perform the action immediately.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When at a sinkbasin, fridge, microwave, etc. with appropriate object.

general_skills.title: Common Sense Object Location
general_skills.principle: Begin search at the furniture type where the object is normally stored (e.g., soapbar on shelf, spoon in drawer).
general_skills.when_to_apply: When starting a task that requires finding a specific household object.

general_skills.title: Examine Open Surfaces First
general_skills.principle: Before opening closed containers, examine all open surfaces (countertops, tables, shelves) for the target object.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When searching for an object and open surfaces are nearby.

general_skills.title: Direct Transformation Then Placement
general_skills.principle: After cleaning, heating, or cooling the object, go immediately to the target location and place it without wandering.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When you have just transformed the object and the destination is known.

general_skills.title: Sequential Container Opening
general_skills.principle: Open containers in increasing numerical order without skipping to ensure systematic search.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When searching for a target object and multiple closed containers exist.

general_skills.title: Transform Immediately After Pickup
general_skills.principle: After picking up an object that requires cleaning, cooling, or heating, go directly to the appropriate station and perform the transformation.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After picking up an object that needs transformation before placement.

general_skills.title: No Examine on Held Object
general_skills.principle: Do not examine or look at an object you are holding; instead proceed to the next required action.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When holding an object that needs to be transformed or placed.

general_skills.title: Open Destination Before Placement
general_skills.principle: Before placing an object into a container, ensure the container is open.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When about to place an object into a closed container.

general_skills.title: Hold Object Through Transformation
general_skills.principle: Once you pick up the target object, do not drop it until after the required transformation and final placement.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When holding an object that needs cleaning, cooling, or heating.

general_skills.title: Search Containers Before Surfaces
general_skills.principle: First open all closed containers systematically, then check open surfaces (countertops, tables, etc.) for the target.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the target object is not immediately visible and the task requires locating it.

general_skills.title: Switch Search Domain After Empties
general_skills.principle: After opening two empty containers of the same type, move to a different location type, e.g., from cabinets to countertops.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When searching for a target object and encountering consecutive empty containers.

general_skills.title: Cover All Container Types Once
general_skills.principle: Before revisiting any container type, check at least one of each other type: cabinets, drawers, shelves, fridge.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the target is not found after initial searches and multiple container types exist.

general_skills.title: Proceed Directly After Acquisition
general_skills.principle: Once you hold the target object, immediately go to the next required location without extra exploration.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After picking up the object needed for the task.

general_skills.title: Surface Check Before Open
general_skills.principle: Move to each container to check its top before opening it.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When searching for an object and closed containers are present.

general_skills.title: Switch Type After Two Empties
general_skills.principle: After opening two containers of the same type and finding nothing, switch to a different container type.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When two consecutive same-type containers are empty.

general_skills.title: Exhaust Open Surfaces First
general_skills.principle: Search all open surfaces like countertops and cabinet tops before opening any closed container.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When you enter a room and need to locate an object.

general_skills.title: Cease Search on Target
general_skills.principle: When the target object is inside an open container, take it immediately and stop all further exploration.
general_skills.when_to_apply: After opening a container and seeing the goal object inside.

general_skills.title: Scan All Open Surfaces
general_skills.principle: At the start, read the initial room description and visit every open surface listed there to check for the target.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the target object is not directly visible upon entering the room.

general_skills.title: Switch After Two Misses
general_skills.principle: If you open two containers of the same type and neither holds the target, switch to a different container type.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When two consecutive containers of one type are opened without finding the goal object.

general_skills.title: Three Empties Switch
general_skills.principle: After opening three containers of the same type and finding them empty, switch to a different location type like open surfaces or drawers.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When three consecutive identical container opens yield nothing.

general_skills.title: Open Before Moving
general_skills.principle: When you arrive at a closed container, open it immediately before moving to any other container.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When exploring containers to find a target object.

general_skills.title: Categorical Target Grab
general_skills.principle: If the seen object belongs to the same category as the target (e.g., any knife for 'knife'), take it immediately.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When an object is visible and its type matches the target category.

general_skills.title: Switch After Non-Target Find
general_skills.principle: After opening a container that contains a non-target object, switch to a different container type immediately.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When you open a container and see an object that is not the target.

general_skills.title: Begin at Countertop
general_skills.principle: Always start your search by going to a countertop, as target objects are frequently found on open surfaces.
general_skills.when_to_apply: At the start of any task when the target object's location is unknown.

general_skills.title: Sequential Container Search
general_skills.principle: After the countertop, systematically open each container in order without skipping any.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When the target is not on open surfaces and containers are present.

general_skills.title: Exhaust All Furniture
general_skills.principle: If the target is still missing after checking all containers, examine other furniture like sinks, bathtubs, and shelves.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When containers have been exhausted and target not found.

general_skills.title: Open Upon Arrival
general_skills.principle: When you arrive at a closed container, open it before moving to another location.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When you reach a closed cabinet, drawer, or fridge.

general_skills.title: Avoid Premature Pickup
general_skills.principle: Do not take an object unless you have a plan to transform and place it immediately.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When an object matching the target type is seen.

general_skills.title: Start at Countertop
general_skills.principle: Begin your search by going to the countertop, as it is the most common open surface with target objects.
general_skills.when_to_apply: At the start of a task before exploring containers.

general_skills.title: Avoid Re-Opening Containers
general_skills.principle: If you have already opened a container and seen its contents, do not open it again. Move on to the next.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When you encounter a previously opened container.

general_skills.title: No Detours After Pickup
general_skills.principle: After picking up the target object, do not wander; go straight to the transformation appliance or destination.
general_skills.when_to_apply: When you have just picked up an object that needs cleaning, cooling, or heating.

pick_and_place.title: Systematic First-Pass Search
pick_and_place.principle: Maintain a checklist of all visible and closed containers/surfaces; open or inspect each unseen candidate exactly once before revisiting any location.
pick_and_place.when_to_apply: After reading the goal and before acquiring every required object.

pick_and_place.title: Grab When Seen
pick_and_place.principle: Whenever a needed object is visible and reachable, immediately take it before moving elsewhere—do not leave targets uncollected.
pick_and_place.when_to_apply: Upon first sight of an unheld object that matches the goal specification.

pick_and_place.title: Transform Before Transport
pick_and_place.principle: If the goal specifies a state change (e.g., heated, cooled, cleaned), perform the transformation at the nearest appropriate appliance before heading to the final destination.
pick_and_place.when_to_apply: Right after acquiring an object that must change state.

pick_and_place.title: Place Before More Search
pick_and_place.principle: When holding any goal object and the target location is known and reachable, navigate there and place it immediately, then resume searching if more items are needed.
pick_and_place.when_to_apply: While carrying a required object and the destination has been identified.

pick_and_place.title: Track Counts for Multiples
pick_and_place.principle: Maintain a tally of how many target objects are required, held, and already placed; stop searching only after the placed count meets the goal.
pick_and_place.when_to_apply: Throughout tasks demanding two or more instances of the same object.

pick_two_obj_and_place.title: Two Objects Means Two Placements
pick_two_obj_and_place.principle: The goal requires two identical objects; placing the first one does NOT complete the task. After each placement, immediately resume searching for the next required object until two are placed.
pick_two_obj_and_place.when_to_apply: Whenever the goal contains "two"; especially right after putting the first object into the receptacle.

pick_two_obj_and_place.title: Remember the Second Location During First Search
pick_two_obj_and_place.principle: While searching for the first object, note any duplicate of the target seen elsewhere. After placing the first, go straight to that remembered location instead of re-searching the whole room.
pick_two_obj_and_place.when_to_apply: During the initial search phase of a two-object task, when a second matching object is spotted.

pick_two_obj_and_place.title: Carry-Place-Return Loop
pick_two_obj_and_place.principle: Carry one object at a time: pick up object A, take it to the receptacle, put it, then return to fetch object B and put it. Do not declare success until both objects are confirmed in the receptacle.
pick_two_obj_and_place.when_to_apply: For pick_two tasks where only one object can be held at a time.

look_at_obj_in_light.title: Seek Lamp Surfaces First
look_at_obj_in_light.principle: Head straight to furniture that commonly hosts a desklamp (desk, sidetable, nightstand) because the target must end up under that light.
look_at_obj_in_light.when_to_apply: Right after parsing a look-at-object-under-desklamp goal.

look_at_obj_in_light.title: Switch Lamp On
look_at_obj_in_light.principle: Issue 'use desklamp' as soon as you reach it so the light condition is satisfied before or immediately after handling the target object.
look_at_obj_in_light.when_to_apply: Upon arriving at a desklamp that is currently off.

look_at_obj_in_light.title: Acquire Or Fetch Target
look_at_obj_in_light.principle: If the target is on the lit surface, 'take' it; if found elsewhere, pick it up and carry it back to the lit lamp area.
look_at_obj_in_light.when_to_apply: Whenever the target object becomes visible, whether under the lamp or not.

look_at_obj_in_light.title: Systematic Surface Search
look_at_obj_in_light.principle: On each candidate lamp surface, look, open nearby containers/drawers once, then move on—ensuring all plausible lamp locations are covered.
look_at_obj_in_light.when_to_apply: After the lamp at the current surface is on and the target hasn’t been found.

look_at_obj_in_light.title: Prevent Action Loops
look_at_obj_in_light.principle: Avoid toggling the same lamp or re-examining the same empty spot; if no progress after one full check, relocate to a new plausible lamp location.
look_at_obj_in_light.when_to_apply: When repeated identical actions yield no new observations or objects.

clean.title: Phase-Ordered Plan
clean.principle: Always execute clean tasks in the fixed sequence: 1) locate & acquire target object, 2) bring it to an available water source/sink to clean, 3) navigate to final location, 4) place object.
clean.when_to_apply: As soon as the goal specifies the object must be clean before placement.

clean.title: Pick Before You Wander
clean.principle: If the target object is visible or discovered, take it immediately; never leave it behind to explore other places, as possession enables direct cleaning and prevents redundant searches.
clean.when_to_apply: After visually confirming the presence of the target object on any surface or inside an opened container.

clean.title: Sink First for Cleaning
clean.principle: Upon holding the target object, go straight to the nearest sink, basin, or faucet and issue the clean/use command before any placement attempts.
clean.when_to_apply: Once the target object is in hand and its required state is ‘clean’.

clean.title: Systematic Container Sweep
clean.principle: When the object isn’t found on open surfaces, iterate through all unopened or unexamined containers in the room before revisiting already-checked spots to avoid search loops.
clean.when_to_apply: After initial obvious surfaces are empty and the target object remains unfound.

clean.title: State Verification Before Drop
clean.principle: Always inspect or infer the object’s state after cleaning; if still not confirmed clean, re-clean before final placement to satisfy goal conditions.
clean.when_to_apply: Immediately after a cleaning action and before placing the object at its target location.

clean.title: Use Location Priors
clean.principle: Begin search at the most probable category-specific surfaces (e.g., kitchenware on countertop/stove, food on dining table) to minimize exploration steps and avoid aimless roaming.
clean.when_to_apply: At the very start of the task to choose the first search destination for the target object.

clean.title: Clean After Pickup
clean.principle: After picking up a dirty object, go directly to a sinkbasin and clean it.
clean.when_to_apply: When holding a dirty object that requires cleaning.

clean.title: Place After Clean
clean.principle: After cleaning an object, go directly to the target receptacle and move the object there.

clean.title: Fridge First for Food
clean.principle: When cleaning food items, begin search by going to the fridge before exploring other containers.
clean.when_to_apply: When the task involves cleaning a food item (egg, pan, etc.).

clean.title: Cabinets First for Clean
clean.principle: For cleaning tasks, always search cabinets first as they are the most common location for items like soapbars, plates, and bowls.
clean.when_to_apply: At the start of a clean task when the target object's location is unknown.

clean.title: Clean Then Place Directly
clean.principle: After cleaning the object, go directly to the destination without any intermediate actions.
clean.when_to_apply: When you have just cleaned the target object and need to place it.

clean.title: Drawer First for Clean
clean.principle: Start search by checking drawers then open surfaces before opening cabinets.
clean.when_to_apply: At the beginning of a clean task when the object location is unknown.

clean.title: Countertop Before Cabinets
clean.principle: If drawer search fails, examine all countertops and sinkbasins next before opening cabinets.
clean.when_to_apply: After checking drawers without finding the target object.

heat.title: Secure Exact Target First
heat.principle: Always identify and pick up the exact object type named in the goal before interacting with the microwave or destination, ignoring look-alikes (e.g., don’t substitute a mug for a cup).
heat.when_to_apply: After spotting any candidate object or during initial search phase; before opening/using appliances.

heat.title: Systematic One-Pass Search
heat.principle: Search each plausible surface or closed container once by opening it and inspecting contents; mark searched spots mentally to avoid redundant revisits.
heat.when_to_apply: While locating the target object and you have not yet found it.

heat.title: Open Then Heat
heat.principle: Upon reaching the microwave with the target in hand, always open the door, place the object inside, and execute the heat action before leaving.
heat.when_to_apply: Immediately after navigating to the microwave with the target object held.

heat.title: No Appliance Before Object
heat.principle: Do not move to or interact with the microwave or final placement location until the target object is picked up, preventing wasted navigation steps.
heat.when_to_apply: Whenever you are tempted to head to microwave/destination without holding the required object.

heat.title: Direct Post-Heat Placement
heat.principle: After heating, navigate straight to the specified destination and place the object once, avoiding extra exploration or detours.
heat.when_to_apply: Right after the heating action completes and the object is in hand.

cool.title: Systematic Object Hunt
cool.principle: Sweep every unvisited surface and open each closed container until the exact required object is found; never loop over already-checked empty spots.
cool.when_to_apply: Immediately after receiving a cool-task and before any object is held.

cool.title: Confirm Object Match
cool.principle: After picking up an item, verify it matches the requested type; if not, drop it and resume the search.
cool.when_to_apply: Whenever you acquire an object but the goal object is still unmet.

cool.title: Prep Cooling Appliance
cool.principle: Locate the fridge first and open it so it’s ready for use before or immediately after grabbing the target object.
cool.when_to_apply: As soon as the fridge comes into view or right after acquiring the target object.

cool.title: Enforce Cooling Before Placement
cool.principle: Do not place the target object in its final location until you have successfully executed a cooling action with the fridge.
cool.when_to_apply: When holding the correct object and before any placement action is attempted.

cool.title: Direct Post-Cooling Delivery
cool.principle: Once the object is cooled, navigate straight to the destination and place it without extraneous detours or re-searching.
cool.when_to_apply: Right after the cooling action succeeds.

examine.title: Pair Objects Early
examine.principle: When both the target and desklamp are seen on the same surface, immediately pick up (or leave) the target there and use the desklamp without moving elsewhere.
examine.when_to_apply: Upon first observation that [Target_Object] and desklamp share the current location.

examine.title: Grab Target First
examine.principle: If you see the target but not the desklamp yet, take the target immediately so you can carry it to wherever the desklamp is found.
examine.when_to_apply: Target object is visible and not yet held, while desklamp’s location is unknown.

examine.title: Shortcut To Tool
examine.principle: Once holding the target, navigate straight to the nearest known desklamp and issue a single USE command—no intervening searches or detours.
examine.when_to_apply: Target object is in inventory and at least one desklamp location is known.

examine.title: Single Toggle Rule
examine.principle: Use (toggle) the desklamp only after the target is in hand or co-located; avoid repeated or premature toggles that waste steps.
examine.when_to_apply: About to interact with a desklamp during an examine task.

examine.title: Explore New Surfaces
examine.principle: If either the target or the desklamp hasn’t been found, systematically check unvisited surfaces/containers instead of re-inspecting places already confirmed empty.
examine.when_to_apply: Location of required object remains unknown after current area is exhausted.

examine.title: Lock In Observed Items
examine.principle: After spotting either required object, do not leave without acting—pick it up (if target) or note its location (if desklamp) to prevent costly backtracking loops.
examine.when_to_apply: Just observed a required object during scanning of a surface or room.

common_mistakes.description: Agent repeatedly revisits the same already-searched locations or containers instead of exploring new ones.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The agent lacks an explicit memory or policy for tracking explored areas, so its search strategy degenerates into local loops.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Maintain an exploration map that records which rooms/containers have been fully inspected and prioritize unvisited or unopened candidates until all reasonable options are exhausted.

common_mistakes.description: Agent decides a closed container is empty without opening it, causing missed discoveries of target objects.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: Heuristic shortcuts or cost-sensitive policies misjudge the effort of opening containers versus the value of inspecting them.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Always open and inspect every plausible closed container at least once before ruling it out, using a checklist of unopened containers in the current room.

common_mistakes.description: Agent ignores or walks away from target objects that are already visible and reachable.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: Perception-action coupling is weak, so detected objects are not tightly linked to action plans that acquire them.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Embed a perception buffer that immediately queues pick-up actions for visible goal objects and interrupts any ongoing exploratory loop.

common_mistakes.description: Agent keeps searching after acquiring enough items because it loses track of how many targets have been collected.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: Internal counters for goal progress are missing or not updated reliably when objects are picked up or placed.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Maintain explicit numerical goals and increment/decrement them on every successful pickup or placement, triggering transition to the next sub-goal when counts are satisfied.

common_mistakes.description: Agent fails to deliver a held target object to the known destination, instead continuing to wander.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: Planning separates acquisition and delivery but lacks a mechanism to reprioritize delivery once an item is in hand.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Adopt a hierarchical policy that, upon holding a goal object, immediately switches to a high-priority ‘deliver-to-goal’ subtask before resuming further search.

common_mistakes.description: Agent completes spatial placement while skipping required state changes (e.g., cleaning, heating).
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The agent conflates object presence with goal satisfaction and omits checking or planning for property predicates like cleanliness or temperature.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Integrate state precondition checks into the planner so that placement actions are only considered valid after verifying and, if necessary, executing the requisite state-changing operations.

common_mistakes.description: Agent repeatedly toggles or examines objects that yield no new information or progress.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: Exploration heuristics do not penalize redundant actions, leading to low-utility action loops when uncertain.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Implement novelty or information gain metrics that discourage repeating identical actions unless the environment state has changed since the last attempt.

common_mistakes.description: Agent mishandles spatial relations (e.g., ‘under’, ‘inside’, ‘behind’) by inspecting only obvious surfaces and ignoring less visible sub-locations.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: Parsing of relational language is not coupled with a comprehensive enumeration of environment affordances that can realize those relations.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: During task parsing, generate explicit search targets for all sub-locations associated with the reference object (drawers, shelves, underside) and iterate through them systematically.

common_mistakes.description: Agent forgets which object it is holding, leading to unnecessary pickups, drops, or misplacements.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: The internal state does not persistently encode the identity and status of the carried object across time steps.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Maintain a dedicated ‘hand inventory’ structure updated after every pickup/drop, and consult it before issuing navigation or interaction commands.

common_mistakes.description: Agent executes inefficient action sequences by searching for each required object serially rather than batching placements or leveraging proximity.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: Lack of multi-goal planning causes the agent to treat each instance independently, resulting in unnecessary travel and toggling.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Use planning algorithms that group similar subtasks, allowing the agent to collect all required objects in one pass before performing consolidated delivery or transformation steps.

common_mistakes.description: Agent prematurely terminates or stalls without having observed any candidate objects that satisfy the goal.
common_mistakes.why_it_happens: Termination criteria rely on step limits or subjective confidence rather than verified goal completion signals.
common_mistakes.how_to_avoid: Only allow ‘done’ actions when explicit goal predicates are met; otherwise, continue targeted exploration of remaining unvisited rooms and containers.

clean.content:
# Clean Task Skill Tree

## Goal Identification
- Parse the task: "clean some [object] and put it in/on [destination]" or "put a clean [object] in/on [destination]".
- The [object] must be cleaned before placing at [destination].
- Identify [cleaning_source] as a sinkbasin or bathtubbasin (typically sinkbasin 1).

## Phase 1: Locate and Take the Target Object
### Systematic Search Order – Follow Exactly
- Read the initial room description. Identify every receptacle type present: cabinets, drawers, fridge, countertops, diningtables, sidetables, shelves, sinkbasins, etc.
- **Search in this exact order**:  
  1. **All cabinets** in increasing number order (cabinet 1, cabinet 2, ...). For each, first go to it, then `open cabinet X` to inspect contents.  
  2. **All drawers** in increasing number order (drawer 1, drawer 2, ...). For each, go, `open drawer X`, inspect.  
  3. **The fridge** (if present). Go, `open fridge 1`, inspect.  
  4. **All open surfaces** (countertops, diningtables, sidetables, shelves, sinkbasins, etc.) in any order. You can see objects on open surfaces without opening – just go to them and read the observation.
- Do **not** skip any receptacle instance. If you have searched all of the above and still not found the target object, re-read the initial description to ensure you did not miss a receptacle type (e.g., a shelf or bathtub).
- **Important**: Always open closed containers (cabinets, drawers, fridge) after arriving. Do **not** use `examine` – `examine` does not reveal contents of closed containers. Use `open` instead.

### Object Name Verification
- Before taking an object, verify that its name matches the task target **exactly** (e.g., "cup" ≠ "mug"; "pan" ≠ "pot"). If it matches, take it and proceed to Phase 2. If not, continue searching.

### Persistence – Do Not Stop Early
- **The search is not complete until you have visited every single instance of every receptacle type present.** Stopping before finishing all types is the most common cause of failure.
- If you have searched everything and still not found the object, re-read the initial description – you may have missed a receptacle type.

## Phase 2: Clean the Object
- While holding [object], go to [cleaning_source] (typically sinkbasin 1).
- Immediately use "clean [object] with [cleaning_source]".
- Confirm the observation says you cleaned it; if not retry or check you are at the correct source.
- Do not use "look" or "examine" at the sink – only the clean action works.

## Phase 3: Place the Clean Object at Destination
- After cleaning, go to the [destination] specified in the task (e.g., cabinet, diningtable, microwave, stoveburner).
- Use "move [object] to [destination]" to place it.
- Confirm the observation shows the object is now at the destination.

## Completion
- The task ends when you have successfully placed the clean object. Do not continue searching or moving other objects.

# Goal: Cool an object and move it to a specified target location.

## Sub-goal 1: Find the object to cool.
- The target object is not yet in your inventory. You must locate it by searching all receptacles in the room.

### Initial assessment
- Start by reading the room description from the `look` command. It lists all receptacles with their numbers.
- Do not assume any receptacle contents are known until you have explicitly looked inside.

### Systematic search of open flat surfaces (mandatory order)
- The target is often on a flat surface (countertop, diningtable, sidetable, shelf, sinkbasin, stoveburner). Do not open closed receptacles until every flat surface has been checked.
- **You must check every flat surface listed in the room description in this exact order, without skipping any.**

#### Exhaustive enumeration of all flat surfaces
- List all flat surface types from the room description: countertops, diningtables, sidetables, shelves, sinkbasin, stoveburners.
- Visit each numbered instance in order: all countertops first, then diningtables, then sidetables, then shelves, then sinkbasin, then stoveburners.
- For each:
  1. Go to it.
  2. Read the observation. If the target is present, take it immediately using `take <object> from <location>`.
  3. If not, move to the next without extra actions.
- **Do not skip any flat surface, even if you have visited it earlier for another reason.**

### If target still not found: search closed receptacles, starting with the fridge
- After every open flat surface has been checked, search closed receptacles. The fridge is both a likely hiding place for the object (if it needs cooling) and the appliance you will use to cool it. **Always check the fridge first among closed containers.**
  1. Go to the fridge.
  2. If it is closed, open it.
  3. Look at its contents. If the target is present, take it. (You are already at the fridge; you can go straight to cooling.)
  4. If not, move on to other closed receptacles.

#### Systematic search of all other closed receptacles
- After checking the fridge, identify every remaining closed receptacle from the room description: cabinets, drawers, microwave (any numbered instances of each type). **Do not stop after a few; you must check every numbered instance.**
- For each numbered instance:
  1. Go to it.
  2. **Use the `open` action to open the receptacle** (do not use 'examine' or 'look' alone—only 'open' reveals the interior contents). The observation will then show what is inside.
  3. If it is closed, open it.
  4. Read the observation. If the target is present, take it.
  5. If not, proceed to the next instance.
- **Do not skip any numbered instance of any closed receptacle type.** If one cabinet is empty, continue to the next cabinet. Only stop when you have checked every instance listed in the room description.
- If after all that the object is still not found, re-read the room description to ensure you have not overlooked any receptacle.

## Sub-goal 2: Take the object.
- Once you see the object, take it immediately with `take <object> from <location>`.

### Immediately cool after picking (mandatory)
- As soon as you have taken the object, cool it using the fridge before doing anything else. Do not move to the target location or do other actions.

## Sub-goal 3: Cool the object using the fridge.
- Ensure you are at the fridge (go there if not already).
- If the fridge is closed, open it.
- Use `cool <object> with fridge`.

## Sub-goal 4: Move the cooled object to the target location.
- Go to the target location (named in the task).
- Use `move <object> to <target>`.

## Completion check:
- The task is complete when the object has been cooled and placed at the target location. Trust the sequence.
cool.critique: The agent partially followed the skill tree but deviated from the mandatory flat-surface order (skipped shelves and stoveburners before fridge) and used 'examine' instead of 'open' to see inside a closed receptacle, causing the search to fail. The skill tree's wording was clarified to emphasize the exact action needed and the strictness of the search order.
cool.changelog: Refined the systematic search procedure to reinforce mandatory flat-surface order, explicitly state that 'open' is the correct action for closed receptacles, and add emphasis on continuing until all receptacles are checked.

round_failures.root_cause: The agent visited many locations but never searched drawers or additional cabinets, so it never found a tomato.
round_failures.skill_tree_gap: Missing a complete search procedure for objects that may be in less obvious places.

look_at_obj_in_light.content:
# Goal: Examine a target object using a light source (e.g., desklamp)

## Phase 1: Locate the light source
- Identify a desklamp from the objects visible on surfaces in your current location. If you see a desklamp, note its receptacle.
- If no desklamp is visible at your current location, systematically search all receptacles you observed in the initial room description.
  ### Systematic search for desklamp
  - List each receptacle (e.g., desk, dresser, sidetable, shelf, bed, etc.) from the room description.
  - Move to each receptacle (action: go to <receptacle>) and examine its contents.
  - Stop as soon as you find a desklamp. That receptacle is now the lamp's location.
- Once you know a receptacle that contains a desklamp, move there if not already present.

## Phase 2: Turn on the light
- Ensure you are at the same receptacle as the desklamp (if not already, go there).
- Use the desklamp (action: use desklamp <number>). The observation will confirm: "You turn on the desklamp".
- The light is now on. This precondition must be satisfied before examining the target object.

## Phase 3: Locate the target object
- After turning on the lamp, first check the lamp's receptacle for the target object. If present, proceed to Phase 4.
- If not, recall the initial room description (the first observation) and list every receptacle it mentioned — include beds, desks, dressers, sidetables, shelves, coffeetables, armchairs, sofas, etc. Do **not** restrict your search to only one type.
  ### Systematic search of all surface receptacles
  #### Search procedure
  - Write down the full list of surface receptacles from the initial description. Every one of them must be visited.
  - Exclude the lamp's receptacle (already checked). Then visit each remaining receptacle **in any order**.
  - For each, use the 'go to <receptacle>' action and examine its contents. Do **not** open any drawer or cabinet until you have visited every surface receptacle on your list.
  - If you find the target object on any receptacle, proceed to Phase 4.
  - After visiting **all** listed surface receptacles and not finding the target, then and only then consider opening closed containers (drawers, cabinets, etc.). For each closed container, go to it, open it, and examine its contents.
- If you have exhausted all surface receptacles and all closed containers without success, you may have missed a receptacle; re-check the initial description for any receptacles you omitted.

## Phase 4: Take and examine the target object
- Take the target object from its receptacle (action: take <object> from <receptacle>).
- The task is considered complete once the object is in your inventory and the light is on.
look_at_obj_in_light.critique: The agent correctly followed Phase 1 and 2 (locate and turn on the desklamp). However, during Phase 3 it did not visit all surface receptacles from the initial description — it searched only shelves and one drawer, skipping the bed and any other surfaces. The skill tree's heading 'Search all desks and shelves for target' may have misled the agent into focusing on those specific types, while the body did include a more general list but the heading itself was incomplete. The failure thus stems from both the agent's incomplete execution and the ambiguous heading.
look_at_obj_in_light.changelog: Renamed the heading '### Search all desks and shelves for target' to '### Systematic search of all surface receptacles' and added a deeper subsection '#### Search procedure' that explicitly instructs the agent to list all receptacle types from the initial description and to visit every one before opening any containers.

pick_and_place.content:
# pick_and_place skill tree

## Goal
You must pick up a specific object and place it into or onto a specified receptacle. The task description states both the object and the target (e.g., "put a book in sofa").

## Sub-Goal Flow
### 1. Parse the task
Identify two entities: the **target object** (what to pick) and the **target receptacle** (where to place it). Keep these in mind throughout.

### 2. Locate the target object
#### 2.1 List all receptacles
- **Use ONLY the initial room observation** to create your list of receptacles. The very first observation after "Your task is to: ..." shows every receptacle in the room. Write down every name exactly as it appears. Do **not** add any receptacles that you encounter later (e.g., sidetables not mentioned initially). That initial list is your complete search set.
- Include ALL types: cabinets, drawers, shelves, tables, countertops, sofas, armchairs, ottomans, dressers, sidetables, desks, sinks, bathtubbasins, handtowelholders, towelholders, toilet, toiletpaperhanger, garbagecan, beds, and any other furniture mentioned. **Include the target receptacle itself** – the object might already be on it.
- Common overlooked receptacles: desks, dressers, armchairs, beds, sidetables, tvstands, countertops, sinkbasins, bathtubbasins, handtowelholders, toilet, garbagecan. Make sure you list every one you see.

#### 2.2 Execute a prioritized search
- Create a mental queue of all receptacles from step 2.1. Visit them in the following order to find the object faster:
  1. **Target receptacle** – the object might already be on it. Go there first.
  2. **Other open surfaces** – tables, desks, shelves, countertops, beds, armchairs, sofas, sidetables, etc. These are visible without opening.
  3. **Closed containers** – drawers, cabinets, safes, fridges, etc. Open each before examining.
  Within each category, any order is fine.
- For each receptacle:
  - Go to it (`go to <receptacle>`).
  - If closed, open it (`open <receptacle>`) before examining.
  - Read the observation. It lists objects inside or on the receptacle.
  - If you see the target object, use `take <object> from <receptacle>`. Then proceed immediately to step 3 (placement). **Do not continue searching.**
  - If not found, mark the receptacle as checked and move to the next.
- If you have visited every receptacle on your list (in the priority order) and still not found the object, re-read the initial room observation to ensure you didn't miss any.
- **Do not** wander to receptacles that were not on your initial list.

#### 2.3 Use object type to guess likely locations
- Some objects are more commonly found in certain types of receptacles. Use this knowledge to narrow your search, but do **not** skip any receptacle entirely – if your initial guess fails, continue searching all.
  - **Electronics** (cellphone, alarm clock, laptop, tablet): often on desks, shelves, tables, or dressers.
  - **Utensils** (butterknife, spoon, fork, knife): typically in drawers or cabinets.
  - **Toiletries** (toiletpaper, soap, spraybottle, toothpaste): usually in bathroom cabinets, drawers, or near sinks, toilet paper hanger, towel holder.
  - **Clothing** (towel, cloth, handtowel): on towel holders, laundry hamper, beds, dressers.
  - **Paper/office** (book, cd, creditcard, pen, pencil, keychain): anywhere – surfaces, drawers, shelves.
- When you begin searching, start with categories that match the object's type, then proceed to the others. This reduces search steps.

### 3. Verify and pick up
- Before picking up any object, **confirm that its name exactly matches the target object** (e.g., if task says "cloth", do not pick "handtowel"; if task says "spraybottle", do not pick "soapbottle"). If there is any mismatch, do not take it.
- **Exact match is required** – synonyms are not acceptable. For example, "handtowel" is not "cloth", "towel" is not "cloth", "soapbar" is not "soapbottle", "winebottle" is not "glassbottle". When in doubt, re-read the task description and the observed object name.
- Once confirmed, use `take <object> from <receptacle>` to pick it up.
- If you are already carrying something else and it is not the target, you may drop it (not typical, but avoid carrying wrong items).

### 4. Navigate to the target receptacle
- After successfully picking up the target object, move to the target receptacle (e.g., "sofa 1", "toilet 1", "garbagecan 1") using `go to <receptacle>`.

### 5. Place the object
- When you arrive at the target receptacle, immediately execute `move <object> to <receptacle>`.
- Do **not** perform any other actions (like examining or going away) before placing; placing is the final required action.

### 6. Termination
- After the `move` action, the task is complete. No further actions are needed.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
- **Wrong object pickup:** Always re-verify the object name in the observation before using `take`. Never take an object unless its name is an exact match.
- **Incomplete search:** Do not skip any receptacle type or instance. The target object may be on any surface, in any drawer, or inside any cabinet. Check all furniture listed in the initial room observation – including desks, dressers, beds, armchairs, and other surfaces often missed.
- **Skipping the target receptacle as a search location:** The object might already be on the target receptacle. Always check it first (per the prioritized order).
- **Not using object type to prioritize:** If the object is a utensil, focus on drawers and cabinets; if an electronic, check desks and shelves first. This speeds up search and prevents overlooking likely containers.
- **Using receptacles not in the initial list:** The initial room observation is the only source of all receptacles. If you start going to a receptacle that was not in that first description (e.g., a sidetable that appears only after moving), you are wasting steps. Stick to your initial list.
- **Giving up too early:** If you have not found the object after checking many receptacles, do not stop until you have visited every single one on your list. Patience is required.
- **Missing the placement step:** Arriving at the target is not enough; you must explicitly `move` the object.

The tree's instructions were clear, so the failure is due to execution, not wording. However, the tree lacked guidance on search order and object-type hints, which the refined version adds.

Also updated 'Common Mistakes' accordingly.

pick_two_obj_and_place.content:
# pick_two_obj_and_place

## Goal
- Place exactly two instances of a specific object into a specified target receptacle.
- The task is complete only when both objects are placed. Do not stop after one.

## Initial Steps
1. Read the task carefully. Identify the exact object type and target receptacle.
2. **Before moving**, read the room description and list every furniture item. Do not skip this step.
3. For each furniture item: if it is a closed container (drawer, cabinet, safe, fridge, etc.), open it now. Systematically open all closed containers before searching further.
   - Do not assume a container is empty until you have opened and looked inside.

## Search Strategy
- **Exhaustive first pass**: Visit every furniture item exactly once. Do not revisit any location until you have checked all others.
- **Never skip a furniture type**: Even if you think the object is unlikely on a bed or in a drawer, check every type. Common failure: only searching one type (e.g., only drawers or only shelves).
- **Use object-specific location priors only to guide order** (e.g., books often on shelves, food in fridge), but **never** to decide whether to check a type. Always check all types.
- After opening all containers initially, immediately begin visiting all furniture items in any order. For each:
  - Go to it. If closed, open it.
  - Look at its contents. If you see an object whose exact name matches the required type, take it (after identity verification – see below).
  - If not, move on to the next furniture item.

### Exhaustive Search Loop (for both first and second object)
1. Mentally list all furniture items from the room description.
2. For each item on that list:
   - Go to it.
   - If it is a container and is closed, open it.
   - Examine its contents (on surfaces or inside).
   - If the correct object is present, take it. If you already have one in hand and are looking for the second, remember to drop or place the first before taking the second? (No – you should not be holding the first; you should have placed it already. If you still have it, go place it first.)
   - If not, proceed to the next item.
3. Do not repeat an item until you have visited every item on the list. If you have visited all and still not found the object, then and only then may you re-check (e.g., objects may have been moved by earlier actions).

## Object Identity Verification
- Before taking any object, read its exact name from the observation.
- Compare it to the required object type. Do not take if there is any mismatch (e.g., "soapbar" vs "soapbottle", "pen" vs "pencil").
- This applies to every object you consider picking up – both the first and second object.
- If you accidentally pick up a wrong object, put it back in its original location or drop it somewhere safe, but do not place it in the target.

## Placing the First Object
- Once you have verified and taken the correct object, go directly to the target receptacle.
- Use the action "move <object> to <target>" immediately upon arrival. Do not issue any other commands (not 'look', not 'inventory', not 'go' elsewhere) before moving it.

## Immediately After Placing the First Object
- **You are not done.** You must find and place the second object.
- Begin a fresh exhaustive search following the same **Exhaustive Search Loop** above.
- **Crucially, do not assume the second object is in the same type of location as the first.** If you found the first on a countertop, still check drawers, cabinets, shelves, tables, beds, etc. for the second.
- **Stopping after one object is the most common failure.** Force yourself to continue until either you have placed two objects or you have checked every furniture item in the room without finding a second.

## Placing the Second Object
- Use the same search, identity verification, and action sequence as for the first.
- When you arrive at the target with the second object in hand, immediately issue the 'move' action. Do not perform any other actions first.

## Completion Detection
- After moving the second object, the environment will indicate success.
- If you do not get a success signal, you may have missed one – continue searching. If you have checked everything and still only have one, re-check the room description for any furniture you may have overlooked.

## Common Failure Patterns (Avoid These)
- Only searching one container type (e.g., only drawers). **If you notice you are doing this, switch to a different type immediately.**
- Stopping after placing one object. Repeat: **the task requires two.**
- Not opening a container before looking inside. Always open first.
- Picking up the wrong object type. Always verify the exact name.
- Taking extra actions (look, inventory, navigate elsewhere) when you already have the correct object in hand and are at the target. Act immediately.

heat.content:
# heat

## 1. Interpret the task
- Identify the object to heat and the target placement location from the task description.
- The heating appliance is the microwave.

## 2. Locate the object
### 2.1 After any move: look
- Perform a 'look' action to refresh the list of all receptacles in the current room.
- Write down every receptacle name you see. Do not skip this.

### 2.2 Exhaustive search of all receptacle types
- Follow this exact order, checking **every single instance** of each type:
  1. **Fridge**: go to it, open, look inside. Take the target object if present. Close after.
  2. **Countertops**: go to each countertop one by one, look at contents, take if found.
  3. **Other flat surfaces**: sidetables, diningtables, shelves (and any other flat surface listed). Go to each, look at its contents.
  4. **Cabinets, drawers, garbagecan, sinkbasin, and all other containers**: open each one, look inside. Do not skip any. Even if you have already opened some, double-check you covered every visible container.
- **Important**: Do not stop after checking only a few items. You must visit every receptacle from your list. If you have not found the object after finishing this list, perform another 'look' (action: look) to see if new receptacles have appeared. Then repeat the search on any that were previously missed or newly appeared.

### 2.3 Object identification and selection
- Before picking up any object, read the task description again to know the exact target object type (e.g., "mug", "cup", "apple", "egg"). 
- Only pick up an object if it **exactly matches** that type. For example, if the task says "cup", do not pick up a "mug" – continue searching.
- If you are unsure, examine the object (action: examine <object>) to see its name.
- After picking up, verify in your inventory that the object is the correct one.

### 2.4 Persistence and common hiding spots
- Small kitchen items (mugs, cups, bowls, etc.) are often stored in cabinets or drawers, not on open surfaces. 
- If you have searched flat surfaces and the fridge without success, immediately focus on opening and looking into every cabinet and drawer. Do not give up after one or two empties.

## 3. Heat the object
### 3.1 Efficient heating method (direct from inventory)
- Once the object is in your inventory, go to the microwave.
- You can heat it while holding it: perform action 'heat <object> with microwave'. This is the simplest method and works reliably.
- If you prefer or if direct heat fails, you can follow the longer sequence: open microwave, move object inside, close, open, take object out, then heat while holding. But direct heat is the first choice.
- After heating, the object is ready. Do not return it to the microwave.

## 4. Place the heated object
- Go to the receptacle specified in the task (e.g., countertop, cabinet, diningtable, fridge, garbagecan, shelf, sidetable, coffeemachine, etc.).
- The destination must be different from the source where the object originally came from.
- If the target receptacle is openable (cabinet, drawer, fridge, garbagecan), open it first.
- Put the object into/onto the receptacle: action 'move <object> to <receptacle>'.
- **Critical**: Do not take the object back after placing it. Stop.

## 5. Completion check and termination
- After placing the object, verify: examine the receptacle (action: 'examine <receptacle>') and check your inventory (action: 'inventory'). Your inventory should be empty, and the object should be visible on/in the receptacle.
- If the object is there, the task is complete. Do not perform any further actions.
- If you ever find yourself holding the object after having placed it, that is a mistake — do not continue; stop and end the episode.
- **Termination rule**: Once placed at the target, stop all actions immediately. No more moving, heating, or searching.

Additionally, the skill tree lacked explicit instructions on verifying that the picked object matches the task's target type, leading to picking a mug when a cup was required. The refinements add an object identification subsection and strengthen the exhaustive search instructions.
